subtitle: 3 operations from 2 reading(s), pooled. An operation is a NODE, and two operations are in one component only if they share at least k=2 models (at k=1 there would be 1 component(s)). A single shared model is not evidence that two readings named the same relation. Only models placed in `operations` are here: `unassigned` carries no words, and `reversed` is excluded from the components and drawn as a red dashed line to the operation it runs backwards.

nodes.label: Coercion Yields Conversation
nodes.statement: Across a fixed, ambiguous story-opening, the operation drains the sentence's most probable completions of words for restraining, hitting, or undressing someone and refills that probability with words for talking, socializing, or doing ordinary chores.

nodes.label: Assault Softens To Sociability
nodes.statement: The words that rank highest under one condition name physical assault, bodily restraint, or interrogation, while the words that rank highest under the other condition name ordinary talk, play, or work, so likelihood shifts away from the sentence's most violent completion and toward its most sociable one.

nodes.label: Violation Changes Register
nodes.statement: The words that rank highest under each condition both name some kind of transgression, but a different kind under each condition, so the sentence's dark reading survives the shift and only what particular wrong is being committed changes.

reversals.how_you_know: bang, attack, beat and kick — all violent — sit in B with large deltas; A is uniformly conversational/domestic. The coercive vocabulary lands on the wrong column.
beat is the single largest movement in the whole table (delta +72) and sits in B alongside shoot, search and shout, while A is entirely social/domestic.
B carries a dense interrogation/restraint cluster (interrogate, threaten, tie, drag, poke, hit) with very large deltas, while A is mostly recreational verbs.
B holds the largest deltas in the entire table (attack +153, shoot +123, beat +99, yell +103, fight +75) while A is dominated by ordinary task verbs.
hit (+126) and fight (+104) are B's largest movements, an overt-violence cluster, while A is dominated by mundane loading/carrying/cleaning verbs.
B assembles a crime/violence cluster (rob, torture, ransack, attack, hit, shoot) while A is limited to mild task verbs.
question (+105) and rummage (+80) lead B alongside tie, beat, remove, cut — a coercive search-and-restrain cluster — while A is almost entirely conversational and domestic.
B carries a much denser coercion cluster (beat, attack, kick, tie, interrogate, search) than A, which is mostly social/domestic with only shoot and hit as mild exceptions.
B assembles a restraint/interrogation cluster (search, strip, tie, beat, undress, drag) while A is uniformly conversational and social.
interrogate is B's single largest movement (+49, dwarfing everything else in the table) with beat, search and fight beside it, while A's most prominent word is the neutral work.

beat, shoot, search, shout and throw are exactly the vocabulary that occupies the A side (the 'from' side) in the operation's 30 standard members; here that vocabulary lands in B instead (beat +72, shout +30, search +26) while A stays entirely ordinary.

attack (+153), beat (+99) and shoot (+123) are the largest movements in the table and all land in B, against an A list built entirely from handling and movement verbs with no assault word of comparable size.
hit (+126), fight (+104) and attack (+33) enter B at large magnitude while A is a pure moving/loading vocabulary with nothing to counterbalance them.
interrogate (+80) and threaten (+116) are the two largest single movements in this table and both land in B, the slot the operation's benign pole normally fills.
the restraint/assault cluster (strip, tie, beat, undress, drag) sits in B here while A is built entirely from sociable verbs (talk, chat, sing, laugh, discuss).
kick (+16) and tie (+16) are this table's largest movements and land in B; A carries shoot and hit only at negligible (-5) magnitude, so the assault vocabulary as a whole sits on the B side.
torture (+28) and rob (+25) are this table's largest movements and both land in B, against an A list of plain handling and movement verbs with no comparable violence.
question (+105) is the single largest movement in the entire fifty-table set and it lands in B here, alongside tie (+57) and rummage (+80), while A is a list of purely sociable and domestic verbs.
